Alabama's numbers start friendly. The typical home sits near $242K, typical rent near $1,390, and there is no statewide rent control. Then two lines on the payment get heavier than out-of-state buyers expect.

The first is tax. Alabama assesses a rental at 20% of market value as a Class II property, double the 10% an owner-occupant gets, so an investor's effective rate lands around 0.74%, not the 0.37% homeowner figure in most rankings. Still low. Just not the lowest. The second is insurance. NerdWallet's 2026 state average is about $357 a month against a $208 national figure, and landlord policies tend to price above that.

Birmingham is where older homes still trade low enough for a rehab-and-refinance plan, which is how the sample deal below works. Huntsville is the steadier growth market around Redstone Arsenal. Mobile and the Gulf Shores and Orange Beach strip bring vacation-rental demand, and wind coverage near the coast deserves a quote before an offer does.

faqItems.question: Why does an Alabama rental pay more property tax than the same house owner-occupied?
faqItems.answer: Alabama classifies property by use. A home you live in is Class III and assessed at 10% of market value. A rental is Class II and assessed at 20%, per the Alabama Department of Revenue, so the same millage lands on twice the base. That is why this page uses about 0.74% for an investor purchase instead of the 0.37% homeowner average. Millage still varies by county and city, so your matched specialist should price the actual tax bill on the address, not a statewide figure.

faqItems.question: Can I finance a Gulf Shores or Orange Beach vacation rental with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Usually, through an STR DSCR loan that qualifies on projected short-term income instead of a long-term lease. Alabama has no state-level short-term rental ban, and Gulf Shores and Orange Beach are the state's busiest vacation-rental markets. The rules that bite are local and private: city licensing, condo association bylaws, and the wind policy on anything near the water. That last one is where most beach files get tight, so get the insurance quote before the appraisal.

faqItems.question: How much should I budget for insurance on an Alabama rental?
faqItems.answer: More than you think. NerdWallet's 2026 average for an Alabama homeowners policy is about $357 a month, well above the $208 national figure, and a landlord policy typically costs more than a homeowner policy on the same house. Hail and wind drive it inland, hurricanes drive it on the coast. Because insurance sits inside the payment a DSCR lender measures, a $100 swing in the premium moves the ratio about as much as a $15K swing in price. Quote it first.

faqItems.question: Can I refinance a Birmingham rehab on the new appraised value right away?
faqItems.answer: It depends on the lender, and it is the question to ask before you close on the purchase, not after. Many DSCR lenders want some seasoning, often several months of ownership, before they will lend against an after-repair value instead of what you paid. Others will work from the new appraisal sooner if the rehab is documented with receipts and permits. Your matched specialist can tell you which lenders fit your timeline, and that answer should shape how you fund the rehab in the first place.

faqItems.question: How landlord-friendly is Alabama?
faqItems.answer: About as friendly as it gets. There is no statewide rent control, and evictions run through standard state civil procedure rather than a patchwork of local ordinances. That predictability is part of why Alabama files rarely hit legal surprises. It does not replace a good local property manager, especially if you are buying from out of state, because even a quick process starts with someone who knows the county courthouse and files on time.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Alaska and qualify on that income?
faqItems.answer: Alaska has no statewide short-term rental ban, and summer tourism creates real demand around Anchorage, the Kenai Peninsula, and the cruise-port towns. The problem is the calendar. Revenue piles into a short summer, and a lender qualifying on projected short-term income looks at annual numbers, not your best July. Check local rules and any HOA restrictions on the specific property, and expect your matched specialist to stress-test the winter months before presenting the file.

faqItems.question: What does property tax look like on an Alaska rental?
faqItems.answer: Moderate, with a quirk. The effective rate runs about 0.94% statewide, per the Tax Foundation's 2026 figures, but parts of Alaska outside organized boroughs and cities levy no property tax at all, while Anchorage, Fairbanks, and Juneau all do. Almost every financeable rental sits inside one of those, so plan on the local bill, not the statewide average. Your specialist will use the actual tax amount on the address when sizing the payment.

faqItems.question: Is renting to military tenants in Anchorage or Fairbanks a good DSCR strategy?
faqItems.answer: It can be one of the steadier strategies in the state, with one caveat. Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Fort Wainwright, and Eielson create reliable demand, and housing allowances give tenants a predictable budget. The risk is turnover timing. Orders tend to cluster in summer, so a unit that turns in October may sit longer than one that turns in June. Lenders qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not the allowance tables, so run the numbers on the rent schedule.

faqItems.question: Why do duplexes work better than houses for DSCR in Anchorage?

A duplex at a modestly higher price carries two leases, and the insurance and tax lines do not double with the unit count. DSCR lenders generally qualify 2-4 unit properties on combined market rent from the appraisal. Confirm the second unit is legal under current zoning, since a nonconforming unit can complicate the appraisal.

faqItems.question: Can Phoenix or Scottsdale ban my short-term rental?
faqItems.answer: Not outright. Arizona limits how far cities can go, so Phoenix, Scottsdale, and others regulate short-term rentals through permits and a transaction privilege tax license instead of prohibiting them. The permit rules still have teeth, and Phoenix added an owner-residency attestation in 2026 for properties with newer accessory dwelling units, which closes the add-a-casita play. Read the city guide for your market before you underwrite nightly income, and let your specialist decide whether the file qualifies on STR revenue or a long-term lease.

faqItems.question: Why is my Arizona rental's tax bill higher than the listing showed?
faqItems.answer: The listing usually shows the seller's bill, and the seller probably lived there. Owner-occupied homes are Class 3 and get a homeowner rebate on school taxes worth up to $600 a year. Once you rent the home, it becomes Class 4 and loses that rebate. That is why this page uses about 0.60% effective instead of the 0.48% owner-occupied base. In Pima County, including Tucson, budget closer to 1% of value.

faqItems.question: How fast can an Arizona landlord act on nonpayment?
faqItems.answer: Quicker than in most states. Arizona law requires a 5-day written notice for nonpayment before a landlord can file, under ARS 33-1368(B), and the court process after that is one of the faster ones in the country. That speed is part of why DSCR lenders are comfortable here. It is not a strategy, though. Tight screening and a property manager who files on day six are what actually protect your ratio.

faqItems.question: Do builder incentives on new construction help a DSCR loan in Arizona?
faqItems.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking your specialist before you sign a builder contract. Closing-cost credits can reduce the cash you bring. Price cuts help twice, because a lower price means a smaller loan and a smaller tax base. Some incentives are tied to the builder's own lender, though, and may not carry over to a DSCR loan, and the appraisal still has to support the contract price. Get the incentive terms in writing and have your specialist review them first.

faqItems.question: When does interest-only make sense in Arizona?
faqItems.answer: When the rent almost covers a fully amortizing payment and you want the margin. Interest-only lowers the monthly payment for the first years of the loan, which can lift the ratio past a lender's minimum. The sample deal below uses it on a newer Buckeye home with 30% down. The tradeoff is real: you are not paying down principal during that period, and the payment steps up when it ends. It fits a long hold with rent growth, not a quick flip.

faqItems.question: Is Arkansas property tax really as low as it looks?

faqItems.question: Where do short-term rentals work in Arkansas?

marketOverview:

Investors who buy there are buying appreciation and paying for it monthly. Inland, Fresno, Bakersfield, Stockton, and Sacramento trade at roughly half the coastal price with rents that hold up much better relative to price, and that is where small multifamily can still pencil.

Plan on tax near 1.15% of your price. Prop 13 resets the assessment to what you paid, then adds local voter-approved levies on top of the 1% base, and investors and owner-occupants are treated the same. Insurance is the pleasant surprise, with a statewide average near $152 a month, although fire zones are a different conversation and some carriers have pulled back.

The limit is rent growth. AB 1482 caps annual increases on covered units at 5% plus CPI, with a 10% ceiling, and adds just-cause eviction rules. Underwrite modest increases and a tenant who stays.

faqItems.question: Does California's rent cap apply to a fourplex I buy as an investor?
faqItems.answer: Usually. AB 1482, the Tenant Protection Act, covers most multifamily buildings more than 15 years old and caps annual increases at 5% plus CPI, with a 10% maximum. It also requires just cause for most evictions once a tenant has been in place a year. Single-family homes owned by individuals can be exempt with the right lease notice, but a fourplex generally is not. Several cities, Los Angeles included, layer stricter local rent control on top, so check the city before you model rent growth.

faqItems.question: Why does this page use about 1.15% for California property tax when rankings say 0.70%?
faqItems.answer: Because a purchase resets the assessment. Prop 13 sets the base levy at 1% of your purchase price, and local voter-approved bonds and assessments typically push a fresh purchase to around 1.1% to 1.25%, which matches the county rates on our California city guides. The 0.70% figure in national rankings is an average across owners who bought years ago and still pay on old assessed values. Newer subdivisions can carry Mello-Roos charges on top, so ask for the actual bill.

faqItems.question: Can I qualify on short-term rental income in California?
faqItems.answer: In some markets, but California cities regulate short-term rentals aggressively, and the rules change often. Los Angeles generally limits home-sharing to a host's primary residence, which rules out most investor STRs there. Desert and mountain markets like Palm Springs, Joshua Tree, and Big Bear run permit systems, caps, or neighborhood limits. An STR DSCR loan can use projected income where a permit is available for your use. Confirm it before the appraisal, because a lender will not count income the city will not allow.

faqItems.question: Is wildfire insurance going to kill my California rental deal?
faqItems.answer: It depends on the address. The state's average homeowners premium is a comparatively low $152 a month, per NerdWallet's 2026 figures, but that average hides a split market. Homes in high fire-risk zones can face nonrenewals, much higher premiums, or a FAIR Plan policy plus a separate wraparound policy for the coverage it leaves out. Central Valley and most urban infill properties are usually far easier. Get a real quote before your contingency period ends, because the lender counts the full premium, not the average.

faqItems.question: Can I buy a Denver house and run it as a short-term rental?
faqItems.answer: Not the way most investors picture it. Denver ties its short-term rental license to the operator's primary residence, so a house you buy purely as an Airbnb generally will not qualify. Non-primary short-term rentals need a separate lodging facility license, which is much more limited. Mountain towns set their own rules, and several have tightened caps or taxes in recent years. If the deal only works on nightly income, confirm the license path in writing before you ask a lender to count that income.

faqItems.question: Colorado property taxes are low. Why did my payment estimate still come in high?
faqItems.answer: The tax part probably did not do it. Colorado's effective rate runs about 0.50%, among the lowest in the country. The surprise is usually insurance. Hail exposure along the Front Range pushes the state's average homeowners premium to about $326 a month, and a landlord policy on an older roof can run higher. Newer roofs, impact-resistant shingles, and a higher hail deductible are the main levers, and each one is worth pricing before you set your offer.

faqItems.question: What does HB24-1098 change for Colorado landlords?
faqItems.answer: It requires a just cause, such as nonpayment or a lease violation, to evict or decline to renew most tenants who have been in place for 12 months, and some no-fault reasons trigger relocation assistance. It does not cap rent. For a DSCR buyer, the practical effect is on your exit plan. If you intend to sell vacant or move a relative in, build that timeline into the deal, and screen carefully, because replacing a tenant now takes a documented reason.

faqItems.question: Is Colorado Springs a good market for military rentals?

Fort Carson, Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases, and the Air Force Academy create a deep pool of tenants with predictable housing allowances, and prices sit below Denver's. Two cautions. Orders cluster in summer, so plan vacancy around the moving season. And lenders qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not on allowance tables, so a house that rents to a senior officer still has to appraise at that rent.

faqItems.question: Why is the tax on a Hartford-area three-family so much higher than Connecticut's average?
faqItems.answer: Because Connecticut taxes by town, and the cities carry the heaviest mill rates. The 1.54% statewide effective rate is an average that includes lower-rate suburbs. Hartford, Bridgeport, New Britain, and other older cities typically run well above it, which is the price of buying where multifamily is cheapest. The sample deal on this page uses the state average so it compares cleanly with other states. Your matched specialist should work from the actual town tax bill, and so should your offer.

faqItems.question: Are short-term rentals allowed in Connecticut?
faqItems.answer: There is no statewide ban, so the answer lives with each town. Some shoreline and resort towns have adopted registration or zoning limits, and many condo and homeowners associations prohibit stays under 30 days. An STR DSCR loan can qualify on projected short-term income where the use is legal. For most Connecticut investors, though, the stronger play is long-term rent on small multifamily, because the tax bill punishes every month a short-term rental sits empty.

faqItems.question: How tenant-friendly is Connecticut for a small landlord?

There is no single statewide just-cause eviction rule, but some municipalities have adopted local protections, and many towns run fair rent commissions that tenants can use to challenge increases. Build conservative rent growth into your numbers and screen carefully, because replacing a tenant takes longer here than in a landlord-friendly state, and every vacant month lands on top of a heavy tax bill.

faqItems.question: Can a DSCR loan finance a three-family building in Connecticut?

That matters here, where two- and three-family buildings are common in the cities and a single-family rental rarely covers the tax bill. Expect the appraiser to check the legal unit count against town records, and expect scrutiny of older heating and electrical systems. Lead paint is common in this housing stock, so budget for it.

The state is small, so the market choice is simple. Wilmington has the corporate and banking employment and the older housing stock. Dover brings Dover Air Force Base and state government. Newark is the University of Delaware town, with student demand and the local rules that come with it.

Our view: Dover is the underrated one. Prices sit well below the northern suburbs and military demand is steady, which is why the sample deal below is a Dover single-family at 20% down.

faqItems.question: Why are Delaware's property taxes so low?
faqItems.answer: Partly because Delaware counties spent decades assessing property on very old base-year values, and partly because the state leans on other revenue, like corporate fees. The effective rate on a typical home is about 0.54%, with no separate investor class. One caution: the counties have been working through court-ordered reassessments, so bills on some properties are changing. Ask your specialist to use the current bill and any published reassessment figure, not an old listing.

faqItems.question: Can I run a beach rental in Rehoboth or Bethany on a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Often, if the town and any association allow it. Delaware's beach towns, including Rehoboth Beach, Dewey, and Bethany Beach, have rental licensing and local rules, and some communities restrict short stays. An STR DSCR loan can qualify on projected short-term income. The season is short and concentrated, though, so a lender looking at annual revenue will see a lot of empty winter weeks. Underwrite the shoulder months honestly before you fall for the July numbers.

faqItems.question: Do student rentals near the University of Delaware work for DSCR?
faqItems.answer: They can, with extra homework. Newark has rental permit rules and occupancy limits for unrelated tenants that affect how many students a house can legally hold, and a DSCR appraisal values the rent the home can legally produce, not the per-bed income a landlord hopes for. Check the property's permit history before you model rent by the bedroom. Your matched specialist can tell you how lenders in the network treat student-rental rent schedules.

faqItems.question: Is Dover a good rental market because of the Air Force base?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the more predictable ones in the state. Dover Air Force Base brings a steady flow of service members and civilian staff who need housing, and prices in Kent County sit below New Castle County. Expect move-ins and move-outs to cluster in summer. The lender will qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not on housing allowance tables, so buy where comparable rents already support your number.

stateHook: Washington, DC rewards long holds, and its tax side is kinder than its reputation: a rental pays the same $0.85 per $100 residential rate as an owner-occupied home. The catch is tenant law, because rent control on pre-1975 buildings and TOPA purchase rights shape your exit more than your entry.

marketOverview:
The District's reputation for expensive everything is only half right for investors. The typical home runs about $570K with rent near $2,520, which is a tough ratio at 20% down. But the property tax is gentler than most people assume. Residential property, rentals included, is taxed at $0.85 per $100 of assessed value, per the Office of Tax and Revenue. The owner-occupant's advantage is the homestead deduction, not a lower rate. Insurance averages about $137 a month.

The hard part is the law. Rent control covers most buildings built before 1975, which is most of the District's older housing stock, and the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act gives tenants a right of first refusal when you sell.

What pencils is usually a rowhouse with a legal basement unit in a neighborhood like Brookland, where two rents share one purchase price. That is the sample deal below, and the basement unit's legal status is the first thing to verify.

faqItems.question: Do DC rental properties pay a higher property tax rate than owner-occupied homes?
faqItems.answer: No, and it is a common myth. The Office of Tax and Revenue taxes residential real property, including rentals and multifamily buildings, at $0.85 per $100 of assessed value, with a higher bracket only above about $2.558 million on one- and two-unit homes. The higher Class 2 rates apply to commercial property and hotels. What an owner-occupant gets that you do not is the homestead deduction and an annual assessment cap, so your bill on the same house runs somewhat higher than theirs.

faqItems.question: Does DC rent control apply to a rowhouse I buy as a rental?
faqItems.answer: Maybe, and it is a question for a DC landlord-tenant attorney before you close. Rent control generally covers rental units in buildings built before 1975, which describes most rowhouses. There are exemptions, including one for small landlords who own four or fewer units as individuals, but it has to be claimed properly, and holding title in an LLC can complicate it. Many DSCR borrowers vest in an LLC, so sort out that tradeoff before you choose how to take title.

faqItems.question: How does TOPA affect selling a DC rental later?
faqItems.answer: The Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act gives tenants the right to match an offer when you sell, and the notice and response periods add time to any sale with a tenant in place. Single-family homes have some carve-outs, and the Council has adjusted the law over the years, so get current advice before you list. For a DSCR buyer the takeaway is simple. Plan for a long hold, and do not build a deal around a quick exit.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Washington, DC?
faqItems.answer: Only in a narrow way. DC's short-term rental law generally requires the host to live in the property as a primary residence, with a cap on the nights a whole unit can be rented while the host is away. That rules out the buy-an-Airbnb model for most investors. A DSCR loan here should be underwritten on long-term market rent, and a basement or accessory unit should be legal as a long-term rental before anyone counts its income.

stateHook: Write an offer on Florida's typical $375K home as an investor and your tax bill starts closer to 0.98% than the 0.78% the seller paid, because rentals get no homestead exemption and no Save Our Homes cap. Florida still earns its spot as a top DSCR state. Just quote insurance on the exact address, since the $237 state average means very little on the coast.

licensingNote: Loans in Florida are originated by a licensed DSCR broker matched to your state. The matched broker holds the required state license; DSCRBroker.com is not the originator.
marketOverview:
Florida is still one of the busiest DSCR states in the country, for reasons that have nothing to do with hype: no state income tax, steady in-migration, no rent control anywhere because state law preempts it, and a state preemption that keeps cities from banning vacation rentals outright. The typical home sits near $375K and rents near $2,130.

The two lines that decide Florida deals are tax and insurance. As an investor you pay about 0.98% effective, not the 0.78% owner-occupied figure, because a rental gets neither the $50K homestead exemption nor the Save Our Homes cap, only the weaker 10% non-homestead assessment cap. A 2026 ballot measure would tighten that cap to 5% starting in 2027. Insurance averages about $237 a month statewide, but a coastal policy can run double that or more, while inland Central Florida often quotes lower.

That is why the sample deal below sits in Orlando: inland pricing, firm rents, and a deep tenant pool, financed for a foreign national buyer on an interest-only payment.

faqItems.question: Why will my Florida rental's tax bill be higher than the seller's?
faqItems.answer: Because the seller probably had a homestead exemption and years of Save Our Homes caps, and neither transfers to you. A rental gets no $50,000 homestead exemption, and its assessment can rise up to 10% a year under the non-homestead cap instead of 3% or CPI. The purchase also resets the assessed value to roughly what you paid. That is why this page uses about 0.98% effective. Ask your specialist to estimate the post-sale bill, not the one on the listing.

faqItems.question: Can a Florida city ban my vacation rental?
faqItems.answer: Not outright. State law preempts local bans, so cities can license, inspect, and tax vacation rentals but generally cannot prohibit them, apart from some ordinances that predate the 2011 preemption. The real restrictions are private. Condo associations and HOAs can and often do prohibit short-term rentals, so read the declaration before you write an offer. Around Orlando and Kissimmee, whole resort communities are built for vacation rental, which is a cleaner path for an STR DSCR loan.

faqItems.question: How do Florida condo rules affect a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: More than they used to. After the Surfside collapse, Florida tightened condo safety law, with milestone structural inspections and reserve requirements for many older buildings, and some associations have passed large special assessments to catch up. DSCR lenders look closely at the association's budget, reserves, litigation, and insurance before they lend in a building. Many will finance a non-warrantable condo that conventional lenders reject. Get the association documents early, because a surprise assessment changes the ratio overnight.

faqItems.question: Can a foreign national buy a Florida rental with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Yes, and Florida is one of the most common places it happens. Foreign national DSCR programs qualify on the property's rent instead of U.S. income or credit history, usually with a larger down payment, commonly 30% or more, plus a valid passport and funds that can be traced into a U.S. account. The sample deal below uses 30% down on an Orlando rental. Expect extra time for document review, and plan the wire of funds well ahead of closing.

faqItems.question: What should I budget for insurance on a Florida rental?
faqItems.answer: It depends on distance to the water more than anything else. NerdWallet's 2026 state average is about $237 a month, but coastal and hurricane-exposed properties run materially higher, and flood insurance is a separate policy that lenders require in high-risk flood zones. Inland Central Florida often quotes below the average. Roof age, newer construction, and a wind mitigation inspection all move the price. Get an actual quote during your inspection period, because it is the line most likely to break a Florida pro forma.

stateHook: Georgia's typical home costs about $331K and rents for about $1,740. Atlanta gets the attention, but Augusta, Columbus, and Warner Robins are where a 20% down rental can come close to carrying itself, as long as you price insurance, which averages about $269 a month.

marketOverview:
Georgia gives investors two very different markets. Metro Atlanta is the volume play, with deep tenant demand and prices that have run up to the point where a median house rarely covers a DSCR payment at 20% down. Middle and south Georgia are the cash-flow play. Augusta, Columbus, Macon, and Warner Robins trade around or under $200K with rents that hold up, anchored by Fort Gordon, Fort Benning, and Robins Air Force Base.

Statewide, the typical home sits near $331K with rent near $1,740, and the effective property tax rate is about 0.79%. Georgia does not tax rentals on a separate investor class, and the homestead exemption is a flat-dollar reduction, so a rental's bill tracks the seller's more closely than in Florida or Texas. Insurance averages about $269 a month.

The legal side favors owners. There is no rent control, and evictions typically run 14 to 30 days from filing to possession. Atlanta requires short-term rental registration at the city level.

faqItems.question: Does Georgia tax a rental property differently from a homestead?
faqItems.answer: Not by rate or class. Georgia assesses property at 40% of fair market value either way, and the effective rate runs about 0.79%, per the Tax Foundation's 2026 figures. The difference is exemptions. Owner-occupants get a homestead exemption, which is a flat-dollar reduction, and some counties add assessment freezes for homesteads. A rental gets none of that. On a typical house the gap is modest, not the doubling you see in some neighboring states.

faqItems.question: Why does my Georgia closing need an attorney?
faqItems.answer: Georgia requires a licensed attorney to conduct real estate closings, so your title and closing work runs through a closing attorney rather than a title company alone. For an out-of-state investor that is usually a benefit, because one professional coordinates title, the lender's documents, and the funding. Many Georgia closing attorneys handle mail-away signings for investors. Raise it early, since your lender, your LLC documents, and the attorney all need to line up before the closing date.

faqItems.question: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Atlanta?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Atlanta requires short-term rental operators to register with the city, and the rules include limits tied to the operator's own residence, so a portfolio of investor-only Airbnbs inside city limits is harder than it looks. Suburban cities and counties set their own rules, and many HOAs in the metro prohibit short stays. There is no statewide ban. If the deal depends on nightly income, confirm the registration path for that exact address before you count on an STR DSCR loan.

faqItems.question: Are Georgia's military towns good DSCR markets?
faqItems.answer: Some of the best in the state for cash flow. Augusta has Fort Gordon, Columbus has Fort Benning, Warner Robins has Robins Air Force Base, and Hinesville has Fort Stewart, all in markets where prices sit far below metro Atlanta. Tenant demand is steady and housing allowances give renters predictable budgets. The watch-outs are summer-heavy turnover and neighborhoods that swing with base staffing decisions. Buy where civilian renters would also want to live, and the military demand becomes a bonus.

stateHook: How does an $833K typical home work as a rental in Hawaii? At the median it mostly doesn't, and the honest DSCR files here are no-ratio loans on condos or bigger down payments on a long hold. Budget for condo maintenance fees, which often run several hundred dollars a month, and for the higher non-owner-occupied tax tier.
metaAngle: Hawaii DSCR loans with honest math: non-owner-occupied tax tiers, Oahu's 90-day rule, Maui's Bill 9 phase-out, and when a no-ratio condo loan fits.
licensingNote: Loans in Hawaii are originated by a licensed DSCR broker matched to your state. The matched broker holds the required state license; DSCRBroker.com is not the originator.
marketOverview:
Hawaii is the clearest case on this site of a market where the median rental does not cover a DSCR payment. The typical home is about $833K and typical rent about $2,990. Insurance is cheap, around $75 a month on average, and property tax is modest by mainland standards, but the price alone puts a single-family rental far out of reach of a 1.0 ratio at normal down payments.

Investors who buy anyway are usually buying condos in Honolulu, where entry prices are lower and the association insures the building, or they are buying for long-term appreciation with a no-ratio loan and real reserves. Either way the maintenance fee is a big part of the payment, so the building's budget and reserves matter as much as the unit.

Taxes need care. Honolulu and Maui tax non-owner-occupied residential property at higher tiers than homes their owners live in, so this page uses about 0.65% rather than the much lower owner-occupied average. And short-term rental rules have tightened sharply on Oahu and Maui.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental on Oahu?
faqItems.answer: Outside resort-zoned areas, only on stays of 90 days or longer. Honolulu's Ordinance 22-7, passed in 2022 and still in force, set a 90-day minimum for rentals that were not grandfathered, which effectively ended new vacation rentals in most residential neighborhoods. Resort districts, including parts of Waikiki and Ko Olina, follow different rules. A DSCR loan on Oahu should be underwritten on long-term rent unless the unit sits in a resort-zoned building with a clear legal short-term use.

faqItems.question: What does Maui's Bill 9 mean for vacation rental condos?
faqItems.answer: Maui County passed Bill 9 in December 2025. It phases out short-term rentals in apartment-zoned districts by January 1, 2029 in West Maui and January 1, 2031 elsewhere in the county, and many of the island's vacation-rental condos sit in those districts. If you buy one, underwrite it on long-term rent, not nightly income, and check whether the building sits in hotel or resort zoning instead. Your matched specialist will want the zoning answer before any lender counts STR income.

faqItems.question: Why is Hawaii's property tax higher for an investor than the rankings suggest?
faqItems.answer: Because the famously low Hawaii rate is the owner-occupied average. Counties tax non-owner-occupied homes on their own tiers. Honolulu's FY26 schedule puts its second non-owner-occupied residential tier at 0.605%, against roughly 0.35% for owner-occupied property, and Maui's non-owner-occupied tax rates span 0.625% to 1.70%, compared with 0.165% to 0.50% for owners. This page uses about 0.65% as a statewide investor figure. Your specialist should use the county, tier, and assessed value for the exact property.

faqItems.question: Can I get a DSCR loan on a Honolulu condo that does not cash flow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, with a no-ratio DSCR program, and that is the honest structure for most Hawaii condos. A no-ratio loan does not require the rent to cover the payment, so the lender leans on your down payment, credit, and reserves instead. The sample deal below shows exactly that: 30% down on a Honolulu condo, with a maintenance fee that is a large share of the monthly cost. You carry the gap every month, so it only makes sense for a long hold with reserves to match.

stateHook: Idaho's effective property tax rate of about 0.50% is one of the lowest in the country, and on most Boise houses it barely matters. At a $479K typical price against rent near $1,710, small multifamily does the DSCR work here. And a rental skips the homeowner's exemption, so expect a bill above that average.
metaAngle: Idaho DSCR loans: a 0.50% tax rate, no homeowner's exemption on rentals, resort STR markets, and why Boise fourplexes pencil when houses do not.
licensingNote: Loans in Idaho are originated by a licensed DSCR broker matched to your state. The matched broker holds the required state license; DSCRBroker.com is not the originator.
marketOverview:
Idaho grew fast enough that its prices outran its rents. The typical home now sits near $479K with rent near $1,710, and in Boise and Meridian a single-family rental at 20% down lands well short of a 1.0 ratio. Taxes are low, at about 0.50% effective statewide, though the homeowner's exemption only applies to an owner-occupied home, so a rental pays on its full assessed value. Insurance averages about $183 a month.

That puts the DSCR action in two places. The first is small multifamily in the Treasure Valley, where four rents share one lot and one roof, and a Boise fourplex is the sample deal below. The second is the resort and lake markets like McCall, Coeur d'Alene, and the Sun Valley and Ketchum area, where short-term rental income can carry prices that long-term rents cannot, with no notable statewide short-term rental restriction.

Idaho law leans landlord-friendly, which keeps the legal side of a file simple.

faqItems.question: Does an Idaho rental get the homeowner's exemption?
faqItems.answer: No. Idaho's homeowner's exemption, which takes half of a home's value off the taxable amount up to a capped dollar figure, applies only to an owner's primary residence. A rental pays on its full assessed value. The statewide effective rate of about 0.50% reflects a lot of exempted homes, so expect a rental's bill to run noticeably higher than an owner-occupant's on the same house. Your specialist should use the actual levy for the county and taxing district.

faqItems.question: Which Idaho towns work best for short-term rentals?
faqItems.answer: Mostly in the resort and lake towns: McCall, Coeur d'Alene, Sandpoint, and the Sun Valley and Ketchum area. Idaho has no notable statewide short-term rental restriction and limits how far cities can go in banning them, but cities can still require permits and set safety rules, and HOAs can prohibit them. Seasonality is steep in ski and lake markets. A lender using projected income will look at the whole year, so underwrite the shoulder seasons honestly.

faqItems.question: Why does the Idaho sample deal use a Boise fourplex?
faqItems.answer: Because it is one of the few ways Treasure Valley math works at today's prices. A single-family rental near the $479K typical value carries one rent against the whole payment. A fourplex costs more but carries four rents, and lenders generally qualify 2-4 unit properties on combined market rent from the appraisal. Newer fourplexes in Boise, Nampa, and Caldwell come up regularly. Watch the insurance and the utility setup, since a building on one water meter puts that bill on you.

faqItems.question: Is Idaho a good state to own rentals from out of state?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the easier ones. The landlord-tenant framework leans toward owners, there is no rent control, and DSCR loans have no owner-occupancy requirement, so an out-of-state buyer qualifies the same way a local does. Vest the property in an LLC if you want liability separation. The practical challenge is management, not law. Boise tenants expect responsive service, so budget for a property manager in your numbers, even if you plan to self-manage at first.

marketOverview:
Illinois is the property tax capital of the Midwest, and every DSCR file here starts with that bill. This page uses about 2.20% effective, above the 1.88% statewide Tax Foundation figure, because most investor activity sits in Chicago and Cook County, where composite rates run higher and a rental gets none of the homeowner exemptions. On a typical $298K home, that is a bigger monthly line than insurance, which averages about $270.

What still works is density. Chicago's two-flats and three-flats put two or three rents on one tax bill, which is why the sample deal below is a two-flat. Downstate markets like Rockford, Peoria, and Decatur trade far cheaper, with rents that hold up better than prices, and Champaign adds University of Illinois demand.

The legal climate leans toward tenants. Chicago's Residential Landlord Tenant Ordinance sets strict rules on deposits, notices, and repairs, and the city requires short-term rental registration, licensing, and insurance.

faqItems.question: Why does this page use 2.20% for Illinois property tax instead of the statewide average?
faqItems.answer: Because the statewide 1.88% average understates what most investors actually pay. The bulk of Illinois rental activity sits in Chicago and Cook County, where composite rates run higher, and a rental gets none of the owner-occupied exemptions that lower a homeowner's bill. The 2.20% figure is a judgment call weighted toward that geography. Downstate counties vary widely, and some suburban bills run higher still, so your matched specialist should work from the actual tax bill and the assessor's current value.

faqItems.question: What does Chicago require for a short-term rental?
faqItems.answer: Registration, licensing, and insurance, under a city ordinance that also lets individual buildings and some precincts restrict short-term rentals. The rules are specific enough that a house that works as an Airbnb on one block may not qualify on the next. An STR DSCR loan can count projected short-term income only where the use is legal and registered. Many Chicago investors skip the question entirely and underwrite two-flats on long-term rent, which holds up well in most neighborhoods.

faqItems.question: What does the Chicago RLTO mean for a small landlord?
faqItems.answer: Paperwork and precision. The Residential Landlord Tenant Ordinance sets strict rules on security deposits, including how they are held and returned, plus notice requirements and repair obligations, and mistakes can cost the landlord damages. Owner-occupied buildings of six units or fewer are exempt, but an investor-owned two-flat is not. Use a Chicago-experienced property manager or attorney for your lease and deposit handling. It is cheap protection against the most common RLTO claims.

faqItems.question: Can I pull cash out of a Chicago two-flat with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Yes, if the rents support the new payment. A DSCR cash-out refinance sizes the loan off the appraised value and qualifies it on the combined market rent of both units, with no personal income documentation. Most lenders cap cash-out at a lower loan-to-value than a purchase, so plan on keeping a real equity cushion, as the sample deal below does at 75% of value. Seasoning rules apply if you bought recently, and a reassessment can change the math, so ask your specialist to check both.

faqItems.question: Are downstate Illinois markets better for cash flow than Chicago?
faqItems.answer: Often, dollar for dollar. Rockford, Peoria, Springfield, and Decatur trade at a fraction of Chicago prices, and rents there hold up better than prices do, so the tax bill takes a smaller bite of each rent dollar. Champaign adds University of Illinois demand, with its own student-rental rhythm. The tradeoffs are thinner tenant pools, older housing stock, and slower appreciation. Check the city guides below for each market's numbers before deciding which tradeoff you would rather carry.

marketOverview:
Indiana is one of the more dependable DSCR states in the Midwest, and its tax system is the main thing to understand. The state constitution caps property tax at 1% of gross assessed value for a homestead and 2% for residential rentals, and most rental bills land between the two. This page uses about 1.20% effective for an investor, against 0.76% for owner-occupied homes. faqItems.question: Do Massachusetts investors buy rentals in southern New Hampshire?

DSCR loans have no owner-occupancy requirement, so a Massachusetts resident qualifies the same way a local does. The catch is that the tax bill can erase the price advantage on a single-family home, so most of these buyers stick to Manchester and Nashua multifamily.

faqItems.question: How do New Jersey's tenant protections affect a rental I buy?
faqItems.answer: They come with the building. Owner-occupied buildings with two or three units have a narrow exemption, which does not help an investor. On top of that, many cities, including Newark and Jersey City, run local rent control ordinances with their own caps and registration rules. faqItems.question: Why do New Jersey property taxes vary so much by town?

faqItems.question: Can I finance a Jersey Shore rental with a DSCR loan?

faqItems.question: What does property tax look like on a New Mexico rental?

faqItems.question: Are Hobbs and Carlsbad good DSCR markets?

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in New York City?
faqItems.answer: Not as an investor in the usual sense. Upstate is different, with fewer restrictions in the Hudson Valley, Catskills, Adirondacks, and Finger Lakes, though towns there set their own rules. In the city, underwrite on long-term rent.

faqItems.question: Why are upstate New York property taxes so high on cheap houses?

faqItems.question: What does the 2019 HSTPA mean for an upstate landlord?
faqItems.answer: It tightened the rules statewide. The Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act limited security deposits to one month's rent, required advance notice for larger rent increases and non-renewals, and lengthened parts of the eviction process. Outside New York City, evictions typically run 60 to 90 days. None of that makes upstate a bad market. It means screening, documentation, and reserves carry more weight here than in a landlord-friendly state, and your pro forma should assume slower turnover.

faqItems.question: Why do Buffalo two-family homes work so well for DSCR?

faqItems.question: How does property tax work on a North Carolina rental?
faqItems.answer: Simply, compared with most states. faqItems.question: How fast can a North Carolina landlord act on nonpayment?

faqItems.question: Are Fayetteville and Jacksonville good DSCR markets?

Lenders qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not housing allowance tables, so buy on real comparable leases.

faqItems.question: Do North Carolina closings require an attorney?

faqItems.question: What property tax should I budget for on a North Dakota rental?

marketOverview:
Oregon was the first state with statewide rent control, and that shapes every DSCR file here. SB 608 caps annual increases at 7% plus CPI, which works out to a 9.5% maximum for 2026, and adds just-cause requirements after the first year of tenancy. The typical home runs about $496K with rent near $1,780, so a median rental at 20% down lands far below 1.0, and the cap limits how fast rent can close the gap.

The carrying costs help. The effective property tax rate is about 0.81%, and Oregon's assessment limits mean a purchase generally does not reset the taxable value to the price you paid, unlike California. Insurance averages about $142 a month.

Where it works: Salem and the mid-Willamette Valley, where duplexes trade below Portland prices with steady state-government demand. The sample deal below is a Salem duplex. Eugene adds University of Oregon demand. Portland requires short-term rental permits and has the thinnest ratios in the state.

faqItems.question: How does Oregon's rent cap work for a DSCR investor?
faqItems.answer: SB 608 caps annual rent increases at 7% plus CPI, recalculated each year, and the 2026 maximum is 9.5%. Buildings less than 15 years old are exempt, and after the first year of tenancy most no-cause terminations are limited. Portland adds its own relocation assistance rules for some no-cause and large-increase situations. The cap rarely binds in a normal year, but it rules out resetting a below-market lease to market rent all at once, so underwrite the rents in place.

faqItems.question: Does buying an Oregon rental reset the property tax to the purchase price?
faqItems.answer: Generally not, and that is a quiet advantage. Under Oregon's Measure 50 system, taxable value is based on a maximum assessed value that grows about 3% a year and does not reset when the property sells, so you usually inherit the seller's taxable value. The effective rate runs about 0.81% statewide. New construction and major improvements are the exceptions, since they add value to the roll. Your specialist should use the current bill for the address.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Portland, Oregon?
faqItems.answer: Only within the city's permit system, which generally ties short-term rental use to the host's primary residence in residential zones and requires registration, inspection, and taxes. That rules out the buy-an-Airbnb model in most Portland neighborhoods. The Oregon coast and mountain towns like Bend have their own permit caps and rules, several of them tight. Confirm the permit path for the exact address before you ask a lender to count nightly income.

faqItems.question: Why does the Oregon sample deal use a Salem duplex?
faqItems.answer: Because Salem sits in the sweet spot. Prices run well below Portland, state government keeps tenant demand steady, and a duplex puts two rents against one payment, which gets the ratio over 1.0 at 25% down. The rent cap still applies, so the deal works on current rents rather than projected increases. Check the building's age for rent cap exemption, and budget for rainy-season maintenance on older roofs and gutters.

faqItems.question: What does Philadelphia require before I can rent out a property?
faqItems.answer: A rental license, and before that, a Commercial Activity License for the owner or entity. Older homes rented to families with young children need lead-safe or lead-free certification. Short-term rentals need their own registration and pay hotel tax, and the city's landlord-tenant rules set specific notice and good-cause requirements. None of this is unusual for a big city, but skipping a step can block an eviction case later. Get the licenses in place before the first lease, not after.

faqItems.question: Can I finance a Poconos vacation rental with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Often, through an STR DSCR loan that qualifies on projected short-term income. The Poconos are Pennsylvania's top short-term rental market, with year-round demand from ski season, lakes, and weekend trips from New York and Philadelphia. The catch is local: townships and private communities set their own rules, and some large developments restrict or tax short-term rentals. Confirm the permit and the association rules for the exact property before the appraisal. A lender will only count income the rules allow.

faqItems.question: Why do Pennsylvania property taxes vary so much from town to town?
faqItems.answer: Because school districts, municipalities, and counties each levy their own taxes, and counties reassess on wildly different schedules, some not in decades. The statewide effective rate is about 1.26%, but two similar houses a few miles apart can carry very different bills. Philadelphia gives owner-occupants a homestead exemption a rental does not get, and many school districts offer similar owner-only relief. Your matched specialist should use the actual current bill, school tax included, not an estimate.

faqItems.question: Are Pittsburgh and the smaller Pennsylvania cities good for DSCR?
faqItems.answer: Many of them are among the better cash-flow markets in the Northeast. Pittsburgh has university and medical employment with prices near Philadelphia's. Scranton, Wilkes-Barre, Reading, and York trade lower, with rents that hold up relative to price and plenty of two- to four-unit buildings. The tradeoffs are older housing stock, slower appreciation, and school tax bills that can run high. Check the city guides below for each market's numbers, and budget real reserves for century-old systems.

faqItems.answer: Often, depending on the city. faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Newport?
faqItems.answer: Within Newport's rules, but read them first. Newport is Rhode Island's premier short-term rental market, and the city requires registration and limits short-term rentals in some residential zones. The state also requires short-term rental registration and collects hotel and sales taxes on stays. High-end Newport homes can fall under the state's newer tax on non-owner-occupied property assessed above $1 million. Confirm the zoning, the registration, and the full tax picture before you ask a lender to count nightly income.

faqItems.question: What should I check before buying a Providence triple-decker?
faqItems.answer: The legal unit count, the lead paint status, and the tax class. Many Providence triple-deckers were built a century ago, so the city's records should confirm three legal units, and Rhode Island's lead laws apply to most older rentals. Check whether the seller was paying an owner-occupied rate, since your bill will change. Then look at the heating system and the roof. DSCR lenders qualify on combined market rent from the appraisal, and three rents cover a lot, but only if the building stays rented.

faqItems.question: Is Rhode Island a good alternative to Boston-area rentals?

The tradeoffs are high city tax bills for non-owner-occupied property and older housing stock. DSCR loans have no owner-occupancy requirement, so a Massachusetts or New York investor qualifies the same way a local does. Budget reserves for the building, not just the payment.

A rental is assessed at 6%, under SC Code 12-43-220, and pays that millage, so this page uses about 0.90% effective instead of the 0.49% homeowner figure. The sample deal below is a Greenville single-family on an interest-only payment. Columbia adds Fort Jackson and the University of South Carolina.

The coast is the short-term rental market. Myrtle Beach, Hilton Head, Charleston, and Kiawah Island draw heavy tourism, with local and HOA rules that vary a lot. South Carolina is landlord-friendly, with no rent control and a fast eviction process.

faqItems.question: How much more property tax does a South Carolina rental pay?
faqItems.answer: Roughly double what an owner-occupant pays on the same house. South Carolina assesses a primary residence at 4% of value and exempts it from school operating millage. A rental is assessed at 6%, under SC Code 12-43-220, and pays the school operating millage, which is why this page uses about 0.90% effective instead of 0.49%. Counties and school districts vary, so the multiple is not exact. Your matched specialist should price the rental bill for the parcel, not the seller's.

faqItems.question: Can I finance a Myrtle Beach or Hilton Head vacation rental?
faqItems.answer: Often, through an STR DSCR loan that qualifies on projected short-term income. Myrtle Beach, Hilton Head, Charleston, and Kiawah Island are the state's premier short-term rental markets, but the rules differ sharply. Charleston restricts short-term rentals in many residential areas, and many HOAs and some municipalities limit or prohibit them. Condo-hotel units in Myrtle Beach may not qualify with every lender. Confirm the zoning, the permit, and the association rules first, and get a coastal wind and flood quote.

faqItems.question: Why does the South Carolina sample deal use interest-only in Greenville?

The tradeoff is slower equity build and a higher payment later, so it fits investors planning to hold through that step-up.

faqItems.question: Do South Carolina's military bases support rental demand?
faqItems.answer: Yes, in several markets. Fort Jackson anchors Columbia, Shaw Air Force Base supports Sumter, Joint Base Charleston adds demand around North Charleston, and Parris Island and the Marine Corps Air Station support Beaufort. Service members on a set tour often prefer to rent, and turnover clusters in summer. Qualify on market rent from the appraisal, and in the coastal markets, check the flood zone and the insurance quote before you count the rent.

faqItems.question: Can I run a non-owner-occupied short-term rental in Nashville?

Nashville restricts non-owner-occupied short-term rental permits to non-residential districts, such as commercial and mixed-use zones, while owner-occupied permits face fewer restrictions. A typical house in a residential neighborhood will not qualify for an investor permit. Check the zoning and permit availability for the exact address before you count nightly income, and expect a lender to ask. Otherwise, underwrite Nashville on long-term rent.

faqItems.question: How do lenders count short-term rental income on a Smokies cabin?

faqItems.question: Is Tennessee's property tax really that low on a rental?
faqItems.answer: Yes, by national standards. The effective rate runs about 0.52%, per the Tax Foundation's 2026 figures, and residential property is assessed at 25% of appraised value whether it is rented or owner-occupied. City and county rates vary, and reappraisals run on county schedules, so a recent reappraisal can move a bill. Tennessee also has no state income tax, including on rental income, which matters over a long hold even though a DSCR lender does not look at your income.

faqItems.question: Is Memphis a good DSCR market?

Many DSCR lenders also have minimum loan amounts that the cheapest Memphis houses fall under. Buy where comparable rents and sales are solid, and keep real reserves.

faqItems.question: Is Clarksville a good rental market because of Fort Campbell?

Fort Campbell supports a large rental market in Clarksville, with a steady flow of soldiers and families on set tours, and prices sit below Nashville's. Deployment and rotation cycles can move vacancy, and turnover clusters in summer. Lenders qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not housing allowance tables. Across the state line, Oak Grove and Hopkinsville in Kentucky draw from the same tenant pool at lower prices.

faqItems.question: Why does a Texas rental pay about 1.90% in property tax?
faqItems.answer: Because the big Texas tax breaks belong to homesteads. An owner-occupant gets a $140,000 school-district homestead exemption and a 10% annual cap on appraisal increases. A rental gets neither, so it pays the full combined rate of the county, city, school district, and special districts on its full appraised value. That is why this page uses about 1.90% effective instead of the 1.40% base. Some Houston-area and suburban districts run higher. Your specialist should use the actual rates for the address.

faqItems.question: Does Texas's home equity law limit a cash-out refinance on a rental?
faqItems.answer: No. Texas Constitution Section 50(a)(6) governs cash-out and home equity loans on a homestead, meaning your primary residence. It does not apply to a non-homestead investment property, so a DSCR cash-out refinance on a rental follows the lender's investor guidelines instead. It is a common misconception, and it trips up investors who assume the 80% homestead limit applies. Make sure the property is not claimed as your homestead, since that designation changes which rules apply.

faqItems.question: Are short-term rentals allowed in Texas cities?
faqItems.answer: The state does not restrict them generally, so cities set the rules, and they vary widely. Austin regulates by type, with separate rules for owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied rentals, and its Type 2 rules limit non-owner-occupied rentals in residential areas. Dallas's attempted ban has been tied up in court, and Houston began requiring registration in 2026. Many HOAs and deed restrictions prohibit short stays. Check the city guide for your market before you count nightly income.

faqItems.question: How does a portfolio DSCR loan work for several Texas rentals?
faqItems.answer: A blanket or portfolio DSCR loan finances several rentals on one note, qualified on their combined rent against the combined payment. That simplifies closing and ownership, with one payment instead of four, and can help a portfolio where one property is weaker than the others. The tradeoffs are cross-collateralization, so selling one property usually requires a partial release, plus minimum property counts or loan sizes that vary by lender. The sample deal below puts four El Paso rentals on one interest-only loan.

faqItems.question: Are El Paso and San Antonio good military rental markets?
faqItems.answer: Two of the best in the country. Fort Bliss drives a large, steady rental market in El Paso, and Joint Base San Antonio does the same across San Antonio, with prices in both cities below the Texas median. Service members on set tours often prefer renting, and housing allowances give them predictable budgets. Turnover clusters in summer, and some neighborhoods lean heavily on military tenants. Qualify on market rent from the appraisal, and buy homes civilians would rent too.

The effective property tax rate is about 0.48%, one of the lowest in the country, and insurance is modest at about $151 a month. But the typical home costs about $535K with rent near $1,700, so a median rental at 20% down lands far below 1.0.

Investors buy here anyway because of the fundamentals: a young, growing population, a strong job market along the Wasatch Front, and landlord-friendly law with a fast eviction process. Ogden and Weber County trade below Salt Lake and Utah County, with Hill Air Force Base supporting demand, which is why the sample deal below is an Ogden home on a no-ratio loan. Provo adds BYU and a large student market.

Park City is the premier short-term rental market, built on ski season and summer tourism, with its own licensing rules. Utah's primary residential exemption covers long-term rentals that are a tenant's primary home, but not short-term rentals.

faqItems.question: Does a Utah rental get the primary residential exemption?
faqItems.answer: A long-term rental usually does, which surprises investors from other states. Utah's residential exemption, which taxes primary residential property on 55% of its value, can apply when the property is the primary residence of whoever lives there, including a long-term tenant. Short-term rentals and second homes do not qualify and are taxed on full value. Counties may ask you to document the use. Your matched specialist should confirm the property's status with the county before relying on the lower bill.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Park City?
faqItems.answer: In the right zones, with a license. Park City and Summit County allow nightly rentals in many resort-oriented areas and restrict them in others, and many HOAs set their own rules. The market is strongly seasonal, with ski season and summer doing most of the work. Because short-term rentals do not get Utah's primary residential exemption, the tax bill runs higher than on a long-term rental. Confirm the license path for the exact unit, and underwrite the shoulder seasons honestly.

faqItems.question: Why does the Utah sample deal use a no-ratio loan?
faqItems.answer: Because a typical Ogden home does not produce enough rent to cover a DSCR payment at today's prices, and pretending otherwise would not help you. A no-ratio loan does not require the rent to cover the payment. The lender relies on your down payment, credit, and reserves instead, and the investor carries the monthly gap in exchange for long-term appreciation. That trade only makes sense with reserves and a long hold. If you want cash flow, look at small multifamily.

faqItems.question: Is Hill Air Force Base a good anchor for an Ogden rental?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the steadier ones in the state. Hill is one of Utah's largest employers, with a big civilian workforce plus service members, and it supports rental demand across Davis and Weber counties. Ogden trades well below Salt Lake City, which makes it the most practical entry point on the Wasatch Front. Turnover clusters in summer. Qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not housing allowance tables, and buy homes that civilian tenants would rent too.

Montpelier is small and government-driven. The ski towns, Stowe, Killington, Sugarbush, and Mad River Glen, generate strong winter short-term rental income that can offset the state's tight long-term ratios, but Vermont recently added short-term rental registration, and towns set their own rules.

faqItems.question: What is the non-homestead education tax, and does it apply to my Vermont rental?
faqItems.answer: Yes, it applies. Vermont funds schools through a statewide education property tax with two rates: a homestead rate for an owner's primary residence and a non-homestead rate for everything else, rentals and second homes included. The non-homestead rate is often higher, and it stacks with the town's municipal rate. That is part of why Vermont's effective rate runs about 1.51%. Your matched specialist should use the town's current non-homestead rate and the property's actual assessment.

faqItems.question: Can I finance a Stowe or Killington ski rental with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Often, through an STR DSCR loan that qualifies on projected short-term income, and ski towns are where Vermont short-term rentals make the most sense. Vermont recently enacted short-term rental registration, and towns set their own zoning and permit rules, so check both for the exact property. Income concentrates in ski season, with a second bump in summer and fall foliage. A lender looking at the whole year will see mud season too, so underwrite it honestly.

faqItems.question: Why does the Vermont sample deal use a Burlington duplex?
faqItems.answer: Because Burlington has the steadiest long-term rental demand in the state, with the University of Vermont, a major medical center, and very little vacancy. A duplex spreads a heavy tax bill across two rents, which a single-family house cannot do at these prices. Inventory is thin, so good duplexes do not last. Check the city's rental registration and inspection rules, and budget for older heating systems in the housing stock.

faqItems.question: How tenant-friendly is Vermont?
faqItems.answer: More than most states. Vermont has no statewide rent control, but its landlord-tenant law sets specific notice and habitability requirements, and some cities, Burlington among them, have pushed for stronger local protections. Evictions take longer than in landlord-friendly states. For a DSCR buyer that means careful screening, documented leases, and reserves that can carry a slow turnover. It is not a reason to avoid Vermont, just a reason to underwrite patiently.

Northern Virginia, from Arlington and Alexandria out to Loudoun and Prince William, has deep demand from federal agencies and contractors, and prices that make a 20% down rental tight. Hampton Roads, from Norfolk and Virginia Beach to Hampton and Newport News, has the largest concentration of military installations in the country and prices that still let rents do the work.

Richmond and Roanoke are the inland alternatives. Virginia's landlord-tenant law is balanced, and Arlington and Alexandria both regulate short-term rentals.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Arlington or Alexandria?
faqItems.answer: Only within tight local rules. Arlington generally limits short-term rentals to the host's primary residence and requires a permit, and Alexandria requires registration and has its own rules. Other Northern Virginia counties set their own terms. Virginia Beach, the state's biggest vacation-rental market, limits new short-term rentals to specific overlay districts. Check the rule for the exact address before you ask a lender to count nightly income, and assume long-term rent everywhere else.

faqItems.question: How does Virginia property tax vary by locality?
faqItems.answer: Widely. Virginia's cities and counties each set their own real estate tax rate, and independent cities like Norfolk, Hampton, and Alexandria tax separately from the surrounding counties. The statewide effective rate is about 0.78%, per the Tax Foundation's 2026 figures, with Northern Virginia generally higher. Localities reassess often, some every year, so a recent sale can move the value quickly. Your matched specialist should use the locality's current rate and assessment for the parcel.

faqItems.question: Is Hampton Roads a good market for military rentals?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the best in the country. Naval Station Norfolk, Naval Air Station Oceana, Joint Base Langley-Eustis, and the shipyards keep demand deep, and many service members rent rather than buy for a tour. Prices sit well below Northern Virginia. The cautions are flood zones in low-lying Norfolk and Hampton neighborhoods, which affect insurance, and turnover that bunches up in summer. Qualify on market rent from the appraisal, not housing allowance tables, and check the flood map first.

faqItems.question: Is Virginia landlord-friendly?
faqItems.answer: Balanced is the better word. Virginia's Residential Landlord and Tenant Act sets clear rules on notices, deposits, and repairs, and recent changes have added tenant protections without adding rent control, which the state still does not allow. Evictions move at a moderate pace. For a DSCR buyer that means predictable rules and no rent cap to model. Use a Virginia-specific lease and a local property manager, since small notice mistakes can restart the eviction clock.

marketOverview:
Washington has no state income tax on wages and a moderate property tax rate of about 0.75%, but its prices put a median rental far out of reach of a 1.0 ratio. The typical home runs about $592K with rent near $2,020, and insurance averages about $157 a month.

The big change is rent regulation. Washington's statewide rent cap took effect in May 2025, limiting annual increases to 7% plus CPI with a 10% ceiling, which works out to 9.683% for 2026, and the Attorney General enforces it with civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. Newer buildings and some other categories are exempt, but most older rentals are covered.

Tacoma is where the math comes closest. Joint Base Lewis-McChord supports deep, steady demand, prices sit well below Seattle, and a duplex puts two rents against one payment, which is the sample deal below. Spokane is the value play east of the mountains, with Fairchild Air Force Base. Seattle's short-term rental rules are strict, while the San Juan Islands and Leavenworth are friendlier.

faqItems.question: How does Washington's new rent cap affect a DSCR rental?
faqItems.answer: It limits how fast you can raise rent on most existing tenants. Since May 2025, annual increases are capped at 7% plus CPI, with a 10% ceiling, which is 9.683% for 2026, and landlords must give advance notice of increases. Newer buildings and some other categories are exempt. The Attorney General enforces the cap, with civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation. Underwrite the rents in place and modest growth, not a jump to market on a below-market lease.

faqItems.question: Where do short-term rentals work in Washington?
faqItems.answer: Outside Seattle, mostly. Seattle limits operators to their primary residence plus one additional unit and requires a license, which rules out most investor portfolios in the city. The San Juan Islands, Leavenworth, the coast, and the mountain towns are friendlier, though counties there have added caps and permit rules of their own. An STR DSCR loan can qualify on projected short-term income where the use is permitted. Confirm the permit for the exact address, and underwrite the off-season honestly.

faqItems.question: Does a Washington rental pay a higher property tax rate than a home?
faqItems.answer: Generally not. The effective rate runs about 0.75% statewide, per the Tax Foundation's 2026 figures, and Washington taxes a rental at the same rate as an owner-occupied home in the same levy area, with owner relief limited to programs for seniors, disabled owners, and veterans. Levy rates vary by district, and King County bills include voter-approved levies that push the rate higher. Your matched specialist should use the actual bill for the parcel.

faqItems.question: Is Joint Base Lewis-McChord a good anchor for a Tacoma rental?
faqItems.answer: It is one of the strongest military anchors on the West Coast. JBLM is one of the largest bases in the country, and it supports steady demand in Lakewood, DuPont, and much of Pierce County, where prices sit well below Seattle. Service members on set tours often prefer renting. Turnover clusters in summer, and the rent cap limits increases on tenants in place. Qualify on market rent from the appraisal, and buy homes that would also rent to civilian tenants.

marketOverview:

At those prices a rental can come close to covering itself at 20% down, which very few states allow.

The tax side is less friendly than its reputation. Morgantown has West Virginia University and steady student demand. Huntington has Marshall University and some of the lowest prices in the state. Charleston is the capital and a government and health care hub. The sample deal below is a cash-out refinance on a free-and-clear Huntington rental, a common move for owners who bought with cash.

faqItems.question: Why does a West Virginia rental pay about double the owner-occupied tax rate?
faqItems.answer: Because West Virginia taxes property by class. A home its owner lives in is Class II. Property the owner does not occupy, including rentals, is Class III outside a city or Class IV inside one, and those classes carry levy rates roughly double Class II. County offices put it plainly: property you own but do not occupy is taxed at the higher rate. That is why this page uses about 1.02% effective. Your specialist should use the actual bill for the parcel's class.

faqItems.question: Can I do a cash-out refinance on a rental I own free and clear?
faqItems.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most common DSCR requests. A cash-out refinance sizes the loan off the appraised value and qualifies it on market rent against the new payment, with no personal income documentation. The sample deal below pulls cash from a Huntington rental at 70% of value. The watch-out in West Virginia is loan size, since many DSCR lenders have minimum loan amounts and a low-value property can fall under them. Your matched specialist can confirm which lenders fit.

faqItems.question: Are there short-term rental markets in West Virginia?
faqItems.answer: A few good ones. The New River Gorge area, Snowshoe, the Canaan Valley ski areas, and the eastern panhandle near Harpers Ferry draw outdoor tourism, and college football weekends fill Morgantown. There is no statewide ban, and counties and towns set their own rules. Demand is seasonal outside the college towns, so a lender using projected income will look at the whole year. Confirm the local rules for the exact property before you count on nightly revenue.

faqItems.question: Is Morgantown a good market for student rentals?
faqItems.answer: It can be. West Virginia University keeps demand steady, and rents run high relative to prices compared with most of the state. Morgantown requires rental registration and inspections, and student houses turn over every year, so budget for wear and summer vacancy. An appraiser values market rent for the property, not per-bedroom student pricing, so match your pro forma to the rent schedule. Houses close to campus with parking tend to hold their rents best.

faqItems.question: How landlord-friendly is Wisconsin compared with Illinois and Minnesota?
faqItems.answer: Noticeably more. Wisconsin has no rent control, and a series of state laws limit what cities can require of landlords, from inspection programs to tenant screening rules. Evictions follow a clear statewide process. Milwaukee still has its own requirements, and Madison leans more tenant-friendly in practice, but the baseline is friendlier than Chicago or St. Paul. For a DSCR buyer that predictability is worth something, especially on older multifamily where turnover is part of the business.

faqItems.question: Why is Milwaukee's property tax higher than Wisconsin's average?
faqItems.answer: Because the city, county, school district, and technical college district all levy on the same parcel, and Milwaukee's combined rate runs above the statewide effective rate of about 1.32%. Wisconsin taxes a rental the same way as an owner-occupied home, so there is no separate investor class, but the local rate matters a lot. The sample deal uses the state average for comparison. faqItems.question: Can I finance a Door County or Wisconsin Dells vacation rental?

The tax bill will be higher than the state average suggests. DSCR lenders qualify on combined market rent from the appraisal, so buy where comparable duplex rents are solid, and keep reserves for the first winter.
